note: ECL registry epistemic record. See _base/findings-ledger.md. Backfilled from 2026-09-29/30 sessions; earlier evidence lives in the project workspace (workspace/docs/lessons-learned.md).

changed: registry: verification mechanism added (@ecl/preset-eu 5.3.1 exact pin, classCheck with a 40-entry drift register)
spec: deep-check.md written — the periodic tile-vs-design-system audit
evidence: @ecl/preset-eu@5.3.1 (identical results, ruling out a version artifact)
ECL ships 95 component packages as SCSS; the preset is the only compiled bundle
findings.summary: Half the registry predated ECL 5.x: 18 of 36 tiles used classes the pinned stylesheet does not define.
findings.detail: The verification target itself was a discovery problem — ECL is modular and ships no per-component CSS, so the preset bundle is the only mechanically checkable surface. Cross-checked against 5.3.1 to prove the drift was not a version artifact before making any claim about it.

changed: registry: 15 tiles corrected against the 5.3.1 class inventory and the component .html.twig templates
evidence: @ecl/<component>@5.3.1/*.html.twig (templates ship even though the CSS does not)
findings.summary: Fifteen pre-5.x tiles rebuilt on the real structures — including a card reduced to a single body and a tabs component that is a link list with no panels.
findings.detail: Notable corrections: ecl-tabs has no tab panels in 5.x (it is __item/__link/__toggle), ecl-checkbox__text is __label, the form-group has no error modifier (the error is ecl-text-input--invalid plus ecl-feedback-message), and ecl-pagination puts previous/next on the item, not the link. Three corrections of ours were caught by classCheck during this rework: two invented classes and one canonical-but-unstyled class.

changed: spec: discovery.origin gained a third value, extension — a class in the design system namespace that it does not ship
registry: button/ghost and language-list labeled origin: extension, tier: observed
registry: expandable re-verified as canon after its demo toggle moved off the extension onto ecl-button--tertiary
evidence: ecl-button--ghost present on cordis.europa.eu, data.europa.eu, digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu (observed 2026-09-29)
ecl-language-list exists only as a site-header sub-element in 5.3.1
findings.summary: Two classes in real production use ship in no ECL release; they are kept and labeled, not dropped.
findings.detail: A third origin value exists so a community extension is carried and filterable without ever being mistaken for canon. Each extension tile names its canonical alternative (ecl-button--tertiary; the site-header language switcher), carries no version stamp — nothing in the pin to verify it against, which is itself the signal — and states the class must be confirmed to exist in the target project before use.

changed: registry: 11 observations recorded across two survey rounds
registry: ecl-mega-menu gap resolved with a citation and a tile candidate instead of a blind deferral
evidence: Commission DG sub-sites confirmed on ECL; standalone EU agencies and institutions are not (12 of 30 probed confirmed)
findings.summary: Commission DG sub-sites run ECL; standalone EU agencies and institutions do not — a structural answer rather than a per-site one.
findings.detail: Also closed an L7 worklist item: ecl-mega-menu is canon in 5.3.1 and observed live on home-affairs.ec.europa.eu, so the deferred mega-menu gap could be resolved with evidence instead of left as JS-heavy-and-deferred.
